messages:
Noah: Hey team, onboarding question dump — sorry! First pay showed base but not the $1,000 relocation in my offer. I thought that was a reimbursement?
Noah: Also I picked the high-deductible plan and want to confirm HSA employer contribution schedule.
Noah: One more tiny one: IT told me to expense my monitor but recruiting said its covered. Who should I file with?
Recruiting Bot: Welcome Noah! Please check your offer letter and Recruiting Slack DM for approval docs. Links: offers.redwood.example, relocate policy https://intranet.redwood.example/relocation.
Maya (People Ops): Congrats Noah. Quick answers: relocation can be structured two ways — a one-time reimbursement (Expensify) or a payroll stipend. Which wording is in your offer?
Noah: Offer says: "Relocation reimbursement of up to $1,000 upon submission of receipts."
Maya (People Ops): That reads as reimbursement. Submit receipts to Expensify with tag "Relocation-2026" and attach the recruiting approval email. Finance processes within 7-10 business days.
Lina (Payroll): If you see a partial amount on your paystub, let us know — sometimes recruiters mark a temporary payroll hold while finance confirms coding. But with reimbursement wording it should be Expensify, not payroll.
Priya (Benefits): HSA employer contributions are fed monthly and start the first payroll after your medical enrollment is active. If you enrolled during the initial 30-day window it becomes effective 1st of next month and employer contribution appears on your paystub as "HSA ER Contribution" line.
Noah: Got it on Expensify. For the monitor \u2014 Sam from IT asked me to buy and expense a Dell 27"; recruiting said they'd ship one if needed. Is there a preferred workflow?
Sam (IT): Hi Noah, we try to ship standard kits but if you already purchased, expense it as "Equipment" in Expensify and tag "IT-Equip". If Recruiting promised a ship, ping @Tess and we won't double-reimburse.
Noah: Cool. Any special expense code I should use for relocation vs equipment to avoid hold-ups?
Maya (People Ops): Please use the policy-specific tags: "Relocation-2026" for relocation receipts; "Equipment-IT" for IT hardware. In Expensify put recruiting approval in the comments and attach PDFs. That helps Finance code it immediately.
Lina (Payroll): Note: reimbursements via Expensify hit payroll as off-cycle reimbursements processed on the next reimburse cycle (not regular direct deposit). They are taxable depending on the policy — relocation reimbursements under approved policy are non-taxable up to allowed amounts; we'll flag it.
Noah: Thanks. If my direct deposit hasn't updated (I changed bank yesterday), when should I expect it to land?
Lina (Payroll): Bank changes must be submitted before payroll cutoff. If after cutoff it applies to the next pay. If you want immediate check, payroll can issue a one-time manual ACH but we need a request email to payroll@redwood.example.
Noah: One final: if I have a qualifying life event (moving for work) can I change benefits outside open enrollment?
Priya (Benefits): Yes, qualifying life events (marriage, dependents, move) allow mid-year changes. You have 30 days from the event to submit a change request and supporting docs. Use the benefits portal > Life Events section.
Noah: Amazing, thanks everyone. I'll submit relocation receipts and hold off on contacting payroll until next payday.
Maya (People Ops): Welcome aboard Noah :tada: Tag this thread after you submit Expensify and I'll confirm the processed status.
Noah: Will do — appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
